text: This is the Cutting of the String, as Aun told it on the north cliff in his last winter, to whoever would hold the other end of a line.
heard: This is the cutting of the string, as Orne told it on the north cliff in his last winter to whoever would hold the other end of a line.

text: Tell it slowly.
heard: Tell it slowly.

text: Count the knots as you go.
heard: Count the knots as you go.

text: Among the lamps you will find the people who were in it: a child with a tailless kite, a gull, a boat with its lamp still lit.
heard: Among the lamps you will find the people who were in it, a child with a tailless kite,  a gull, a boat with its lamp still lit.

text: I was the one with the knife.
heard: I was the one with the knife.

text: I was a boy when Ennu gave me a tailless kite, cut from a sail too old to hold a boat.
heard: I was a boy when Inuk gave me a tailless kite, cut from a sail, too old to hold a boat.

text: It had two sticks and a bridle and no tail, so it spun and dropped and would not learn the wind.
heard: It had two sticks and a bridle and no tail, so it spun and dropped and would not learn  the wind.

text: I learned it on the cliff, fist by fist.
heard: I learned it on the cliff, fist by fist.

text: Then I wanted more than the wind's lesson.
heard: Then I wanted more than the wind's lesson.

text: I wanted to know its end.
heard: I wanted to know its end.

text: Mother Hesk sat at the pole with her spindle, drawing the string thin and winding it on the whorl so the islands would not drift.
heard: Mother Hesc sat at the pole with her spindle, drawing the string thin, and winding it on  the wall, so the islands would not drift.

text: I came up the cliff with my knife in my belt, and she did not look round.
heard: I came up the cliff with my knife in my belt and she did not look round.

text: She said only, Mind the thread, Aun.
heard: She said only,  Mind the thread, Horne.

text: I said I would mind the wind.
heard: I said, I would mind the wind.

text: Hesk wound every string the islands flew, and kept count of each knot in her two hands.
heard: Hursk wound every string the islands flew, and kept count of each knot in her two hands.

text: I cut at the pole, and the sky went up with a crack like a sail filling.
heard: I cut at the pole, and the sky went up with a crack, like a sail filling.

text: Hesk did not stop counting.
heard: HESK did not stop counting.

text: Her fingers went on knotting while the sky ran off.
heard: Her fingers went on knotting while the sky ran off.

text: I have never known whether that was cruelty or love, and I have had long winters to decide.
heard: I have never known whether that was cruelty or love, and I have had long winters to decide.

text: When I cut, Hesk's drop spindle slipped from her fingers in the wind and went over the edge of the pole.
heard: When I cut, Hesk's drop spindle slipped from her fingers in the wind and went over  the edge of the pole.

text: The new thread, the one that would have held the sky close, went after it.
heard: The new thread, the one that would have held the sky close, went after it.

text: Somewhere below, I heard it strike the shingle.
heard: Somewhere below, I heard it strike the shingle.

text: Nobody has spun the sky since.
heard: Nobody has spun the sky since.

text: We have only the old string, and it is short.
heard: We have only the old string, and it is short.

text: I sent my word up to Vel, the Upper Sea, on a gull named Hilun, who carried messages between the islands and the sky.
heard: I sent my word up to Vel, the upper sea, on a gull named Hylun who carried messages between  the islands and the sky.

text: She flew so close to the Gale that Tavo grew fond of her, and fond is a dangerous thing in a wind.
heard: She flew so close to the gale that Tevo grew fond of her, and fond is a dangerous thing in a wind.

text: I asked her to tell the sky to come back.
heard: I asked her to tell the sky to come back.

text: She came down with Tavo's laugh in her feathers and no answer in her beak.
heard: She came down with Tavo's laugh in her feathers and no answer in her beak.

text: Sekra was the first gull to follow me up the cut string.
heard: Sacra was the first gull to follow me up the cut string.

text: She wanted to see where the wind went too, and I did not send her back.
heard: She wanted to see where the wind went too, and I did not send her back.

text: She flew so high that frost stiffened her wings.
heard: She flew so high that frost stiffened her wings.

text: I watched her go white against the blue, still climbing, and I did not call her down.
heard: I watched her go white against the blue, still climbing, and I did not call her down.

text: I was glad of company.
heard: I was glad of company.

text: I am not glad now.
heard: I am not glad now.

text: I cut it because I wanted to know how far the wind went.
heard: I cut it, because I wanted to know how far the wind went.

text: That was the whole reason, and it was a poor one.
heard: That was the whole reason, and it was a poor one.

text: The sky drifted off with me holding the knife, and every kite I had flown on that string went with it.
heard: The sky drifted off with me holding the knife, and every kite I had flown on that string  went with it.

text: My hands still remember the line.
heard: My hands still remember the line.

text: For a long time I was proud of the question.
heard: For a long time, I was proud of the question.

text: I did not cut it clean.
heard: I did not cut it clean.

text: The Sun-Kite was still tied to my wrist, so it went up with the others, and its ribbon came loose and streamed away across the Lamp Road.
heard: The sun kite was still tied to my wrist, so it went up with the others, and its ribbon  came loose and streamed away across the lamp road.

text: Ennu had sewn that kite to carry the sun through the year.
heard: Manna had sewn that kite to carry the sun through the year.

text: Now the people of the islands reckon the year by a ribbon they cannot reach, and I am the one who tied it on.
heard: Now the people of the islands reckon the year by a ribbon they cannot reach,  and I am the one who tied it on.

text: Sil ran after the sky along the tide, my sister, the Moon, with her skirts in the wrack and her voice going up the wind.
heard: Sil ran after the sky along the tide, my sister the moon, with her skirts in the rack and  her voice going up the wind.

text: Before I could let go, I had tied a stone to the last line, as if a stone could keep a sky.
heard: Before I could let go, I had tied a stone to the last line, as if a stone could keep a sky.

text: I still feel the weight in my palm.
heard: I still feel the weight in my palm.

text: She is searching still.
heard: She is searching still.

text: Each night she comes up low over the water, looking for a brother who will not be found.
heard: Each night she comes up low over the water, looking for a brother who will not be found.

text: Tirun came home keel-up on a grey morning, with no crew in her and no oars shipped.
heard: Tyran came home keel up on a grey morning, with no crew in her and no oars shipped.

text: The women of the north shore turned her with ropes and found her lamps still lit underneath.
heard: The women of the North Shore turned her with ropes and found her lamps still lit underneath.

text: They asked me why the sky had no lamp for her.
heard: They asked me why the sky had no lamp for her.

text: I had no answer.
heard: I had no answer.

text: Nobody had counted her: not the sea, not the Reel, not me.
heard: Nobody had counted her, not the sea, not the real, not me.

text: When a child goes into the sea, the mother climbs to the cliff on the first still day, when the wind has finally let go of the water.
heard: When a child goes into the sea, the mother climbs to the cliff, on the first still day, when the wind has finally let go of the water.

text: She ties a small kite and flies it over the rocks, so the child has something to look for.
heard: She ties a small kite and flies it over the rocks, so the child has something to look for.

text: I have watched a hundred mothers do it.
heard: I have watched a hundred mothers do it.

text: I have no child to fly one for.
heard: I have no child to fly one for.

text: I had only a string, and I chose to cut it.
heard: I had only a string, and I chose to cut it.

text: Ennu sat on the cliff with a bone needle and a bolt of sailcloth, making a gull for a woman whose husband had gone out and not come back.
heard: Enoch sat on the cliff with a bone needle and a bolt of sailcloth,  making a gull for a woman whose husband had gone out and not come back.

text: I held the cloth taut for him.
heard: I held the cloth taught for him.

text: He asked me to hold it straight.
heard: He asked me to hold it straight.

text: I did not.
heard: I did not.

text: I was thinking of the sky, and the seam went crooked, and that gull still flies with a list to one side.
heard: I was thinking of the sky, and the seam went crooked, and that gull still flies with a list to one side.

text: The first things past the last lamp were the drowned, and none of them knew the way.
heard: The first things past the last lamp were the drowned, and none of them knew the way.

text: A boatman of the Upper Sea, grey-bearded, took them across for nothing, because the crossing is unpaid.
heard: A boatman of the upper sea, grey-bearded, took them across for nothing, because the  crossing is unpaid.

text: I went down to the water and asked for passage.
heard: I went down to the water and asked for passage.

text: He told me I had not drowned, so I had no fare.
heard: He told me I had not drowned, so I had no fair.

text: He was not unkind.
heard: He was not unkind.

text: He was counting, as Hesk counts, and I was not on his list.
heard: He was counting as his counts, and I was not on his list.

text: The sky went up but did not come all the way free.
heard: The sky went up, but did not come all the way free.

text: A short length of cord stayed knotted to my hand, and it still hangs at the bottom of the Unflown, where the wind does not come back.
heard: A short length of cord stayed knotted to my hand, and it still hangs at the bottom of  the unflown, where the wind does not come back.

text: I hold the other end.
heard: I hold the other end.

text: Each night I tell the sky what I did, and each night it does not answer.
heard: Each night I tell the sky what I did, and each night it does not answer.

text: Fly back, I say.
heard: Fly back, I say.

text: I am still holding the knife.
heard: I am still holding the knife.
